transcript.text: my washin mashine wont turn on at all no lights nothin

A washing machine with no lights or response at all is usually caused by a loss of mains power rather than an internal fault. The most common reasons are that the socket isn't live, the plug or lead is faulty, or a fuse has blown. Before we look inside the appliance, please confirm if it's plugged in and test the wall socket with another device to ensure it's working.
its built in behind a cupboard door so i cant see the plug. but my kettle and fridge work fine in the kitchen

Since your kettle and fridge work, the general kitchen power is fine. However, built-in appliances are often connected to a dedicated 'switched spur'—a small isolator switch mounted on the wall near the cupboard—or use a fused connection unit that might have tripped or been switched off. Please check if there is a small switch on the wall nearby and ensure it is in the 'on' position, or look for a small fuse box/spur unit and check if its fuse has blown.
ok i looked and theres a row of switches above the worktop, one says washer and its OFF. my flatmate must of switched it off when she was cleaning. shall i turn it back on?

[Heading: Likely cause: power switch]
Yes, please turn that switch back on. It is very likely that was the only issue. Once you have done so, let me know if the display lights up and the machine responds normally. To be thorough in case there is a secondary fault or to help identify any specific parts if it still doesn't work, could you also check the rating plate inside the door rim or on the back of the door and tell me the make and model number?
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
ok i turned it back on and the machine lights up and works now. i cant find the model number tho, its built in behind the cupboard door and the brand name on the edge is worn off

[Heading: Likely cause: power switch]
That is excellent news—it sounds like your flatmate simply turned off the isolator switch while cleaning. To stop this from happening again, you might want to cover that 'washer' switch with a piece of tape or a small label so it's clear it shouldn't be touched. Is there anything else I can help you with today?

candidates: No mains power reaching the machine (socket, plug, lead, or fuse) (high)
Faulty mains filter or internal wiring connection (medium)
Failed main PCB power supply section (low)
